memos.risk:
Risk officer view: I'd refuse this one, or at minimum skip it. Several flags stand out.

The curve data is contradictory and suspicious: bundle_share at 1.0 (every early buy bundled), top3_share at 0.87, and completer_share above 1.0. That points to coordinated early buying, not organic demand. The brief labels it ORGANIC, but the curve metrics don't support that.

Price action is weak: a 48% drawdown from the 30-minute high, a -34% return over the last 15 minutes, and sells outnumbering buys in that window (455 SOL sold vs 437 bought).

Pool depth is 124 SOL, so a $20 ticket is small relative to the pool, but the 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost is a meaningful hurdle against a coin already in a steep dip.

Refusal conditions: any bundle_share or top3_share this high, negative net flow during a dip, or a drawdown this deep with sellers dominating. If the desk insists on a position anyway, cap at $5, stop at 20%, hold no more than 15 minutes.
memos.scout:
There is no honest case for buying AMM right now.

The strongest-looking signals are weak on inspection. Last 15 minutes show 1,903 buyers against 436.87 SOL of buys, but sellers (1,093) took out 455.54 SOL, so net flow is negative (-18.68 SOL) and the price is down 34% in that window. The coin is 48% off its 30-minute high.

The curve data is a red flag: bundle_share of 1.0 and top3_share of 0.87 mean the early supply was concentrated and bundled, and the completer share above 1.0 suggests the graduation was pushed through by a small set of wallets. Early post-graduation sell pressure is high (sell-to-buy ratio 0.87), and the top 5 buyers hold 31% of early buying.

Nothing in the brief shows demand that will persist for 30-60 minutes. The name "Actively Managed Meme" suggests a promise of management that the desk cannot verify, so I treat it as no evidence. With fees of 1.4-5.1% and a base rate of roughly 20% loss per trade for coins in this window, the expected value is negative. Recommendation: skip.
memos.skeptic:
Most likely loss: a late exit into a fading distribution. AMM is down 34% over the last 15 minutes and 48% off its 30-minute high, with net flow of -18.7 SOL. Sellers (1,093) outnumber the 1,903 buyers in that window, and sell SOL (455.5) is nearly equal to buy SOL (436.9), so buyers are not absorbing supply. The sell-to-buy ratio in the first two minutes after graduation was 0.87, meaning early holders were already taking profit into the launch.

The curve data flags insider concentration: bundle_share is 1.0 and top3_share is 0.87, with a completer_share above 1. The first-two-minute buyers (ex-agent) were 443 wallets for 158.5 SOL, but a launch bot was present, so that broad base may be automated sniping rather than organic demand.

With a 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost on a $20 ticket and a pool of only 124 SOL, any bounce is likely to be eaten by fees and impact. The desk should skip.
